agents.label: Design QA
agents.summary: The page is not rendering any event microsite content — both desktop and mobile screenshots show only a bare '403 Forbidden' nginx/server error page. There is no layout, branding, hero, CTA, or any required element visible. This page cannot be reviewed for design quality and must not be published in its current state.

findings.location: Layout & grid · Entire page, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: The server is returning a 403 Forbidden error. The only visible content is a centered plain-text heading '403 Forbidden' on a white background. No microsite layout, grid, sections, cards, or any event content is present.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the server/hosting access configuration that is blocking the page from being served. Check file permissions, CDN origin rules, or authentication middleware preventing public access to the HTML/assets.
findings.fix_prompt: Check your hosting provider's access control settings and ensure the event microsite's root directory and all asset paths are publicly readable. Remove or correct any IP allowlist, HTTP auth, or CDN rule that is returning a 403 status to unauthenticated visitors.

findings.location: Typography · Entire page, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: No brand typography (Archivo, Inter) is in use. The only text rendered is the browser-default serif bold '403 Forbidden' heading generated by the server error response. None of the defined type scale sizes are applied.
findings.recommendation: Restore the microsite page so that the correct HTML, CSS, and font assets are served.
findings.fix_prompt: Fix the 403 server error so the actual event microsite HTML is served; the page's existing Archivo/Inter font stack and type scale will then render correctly.

findings.location: Spacing & rhythm · Entire page, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: No spacing system is visible. The error page contains a single centered heading with no padding, sections, or rhythm. The defined spacing scale (4–96 px) cannot be evaluated.
findings.recommendation: Restore the microsite so spacing and rhythm can be reviewed.
findings.fix_prompt: Fix the 403 server error so the actual event microsite HTML is served; the spacing scale will then be evaluable.

findings.location: Visual hierarchy · Entire page, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: There is no visual hierarchy. The required hierarchy (event name → value proposition → date/location → primary CTA) is entirely absent. The registration CTA — the most critical interactive element — does not exist on the rendered page.
findings.recommendation: The microsite must be served correctly before hierarchy can be established. Once live, verify that all required elements per brand config appear above the fold in the prescribed visual order.
findings.fix_prompt: Fix the 403 server error so the actual event microsite HTML is served. Then ensure the hero section contains: (1) event name 'WorkX 2026' as the largest heading, (2) a value proposition subheading, (3) date and venue, and (4) a high-contrast '#FF5A36' registration CTA button — all visible without scrolling on a 1440px desktop viewport.

findings.location: Consistency · Entire page, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: No components, buttons, cards, icons, or repeated elements are present to evaluate consistency. The page renders only a server error message.
findings.recommendation: Restore the microsite so component consistency can be reviewed.
findings.fix_prompt: Fix the 403 server error so the actual event microsite HTML is served; component consistency can then be audited.

findings.location: Responsive integrity · Entire page, desktop (1440px) and mobile (390px)
findings.issue: Both desktop and mobile screenshots show identical 403 error pages with no microsite content. Responsive behavior, stacking, touch targets, and hero legibility on narrow screens cannot be evaluated because no content is rendered.
findings.recommendation: Restore the microsite so responsive behavior can be reviewed across breakpoints.
findings.fix_prompt: Fix the 403 server error so the actual event microsite HTML is served on both desktop and mobile viewports.

findings.location: Visual accessibility · Entire page, desktop and mobile
findings.issue: No microsite content is visible, so contrast ratios over imagery, CTA affordances, focus indicators, and text legibility cannot be assessed. The only rendered text ('403 Forbidden' in browser-default bold serif on white) has no brand treatment and no accessibility provisions.
findings.recommendation: Restore the microsite so visual accessibility can be reviewed. Once live, also add a lang attribute to the HTML element (flagged by axe-core) and ensure all content is wrapped in landmark regions.
findings.fix_prompt: Fix the 403 server error so the actual event microsite HTML is served. Then add lang="en" to the <html> tag, wrap all page content in a <main> landmark, and verify that all text-over-image elements have a dark overlay or scrim achieving at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against overlaid text.

agents.label: Brand Compliance
agents.summary: The page provided for review is a bare server-generated 403 Forbidden error page, not the WorkX 2026 event microsite. No brand elements, content, or required checklist items are visible whatsoever. Publishing this URL in its current state would expose a broken, unbranded server error to prospective attendees, which is an organizational embarrassment. Missing required elements: Event name and dates in the hero; Venue / location; Primary registration CTA above the fold; IQPC or portal brand logo; Privacy policy link in footer.

findings.issue: The URL returns a 403 Forbidden HTTP error served directly by the web server (nginx/Apache default error page). The event microsite is either not deployed, access-restricted incorrectly, or pointed at the wrong origin. Zero brand, content, or legal elements are present.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the server-side access configuration (check directory permissions, server block/virtual host config, and deployment pipeline) so the actual microsite HTML is served. Do not publish or share this URL until the correct page loads with a 200 response.
findings.fix_prompt: The deployment target is returning a 403 Forbidden error. Check your web server configuration: ensure the document root points to the correct build output directory, that directory index files (index.html) exist and are readable by the server process, and that no IP allowlist or auth guard is blocking public access. Re-deploy the WorkX 2026 microsite build and confirm a 200 OK response with the full page HTML before re-running brand compliance review.

agents.label: SEO Audit
agents.summary: The page is returning a 403 Forbidden HTTP error, meaning no actual event content is being served or indexed. There is zero SEO value present: no title, no meta description, no canonical, no Open Graph tags, no structured data, and no visible page content. Until the access restriction is resolved, no qualitative or keyword analysis is possible.

findings.issue: Missing meta description.
findings.recommendation: Add a compelling 150–160 char meta description with a registration hook.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a meta description tag (150-160 characters) summarizing the event value proposition and ending with a registration call to action.

findings.issue: Missing og:image — link shares on LinkedIn/social render without a preview card image.
findings.recommendation: Add og:image (1200×630) plus og:title and og:description.
findings.fix_prompt: Add Open Graph tags to this page: og:title, og:description, and og:image pointing to a 1200x630 share image.

findings.issue: Missing canonical URL.
findings.recommendation: Add <link rel="canonical"> to prevent duplicate-content dilution.
findings.fix_prompt: Add a <link rel="canonical"> tag pointing to this page's primary URL.

findings.issue: No schema.org Event structured data (JSON-LD) — the page cannot earn event rich results in Google.
findings.recommendation: Add Event JSON-LD with name, dates, location, organizer, and offers.
findings.fix_prompt: Add the schema.org Event JSON-LD provided in the QA report to this page inside a <script type="application/ld+json"> tag in the <head>.

findings.issue: The URL https://www.ssonetwork.com/events-workx returns a 403 Forbidden response. The server is actively blocking access to the resource, so no content, metadata, or structured data is delivered to users or crawlers.
findings.recommendation: Diagnose and resolve the server-side access restriction (check directory permissions, .htaccess rules, WAF/CDN IP-blocking rules, and authentication middleware). Confirm the page is publicly accessible before any further SEO work is undertaken.
findings.fix_prompt: Investigate the web server and CDN configuration for https://www.ssonetwork.com/events-workx. Remove or adjust any rule that returns a 403 status for unauthenticated or crawler requests. Verify the fix by requesting the URL with curl -I and confirming a 200 OK response before re-running SEO checks.

findings.issue: The page title is '403 Forbidden' (13 characters). This is a server error string, not a descriptive event title. It provides no keyword signal and would appear as '403 Forbidden' in SERPs if the page were crawled.
findings.recommendation: Once the 403 is resolved, replace the title with a descriptive, keyword-rich event title within 60 characters (see improved_meta below).
findings.fix_prompt: Replace <title>403 Forbidden</title> with <title>WorkX 2026 | Future of Work Summit – SSO Network</title> once the page is publicly accessible.

findings.issue: No meta description exists. Search engines will have no snippet text to display, reducing click-through rate if the page ever gets indexed.
findings.recommendation: Add a compelling 150–160 character meta description summarising the event value proposition, dates, and location once those facts are confirmed on the live page.
findings.fix_prompt: Add <meta name='description' content='[Insert 150-160 char description matching live page facts]'> inside <head>. Use the improved_meta.meta_description value below as a placeholder template, updating with real event details from the live page.

findings.issue: No canonical URL is declared. Without a canonical, duplicate or near-duplicate versions of the page (HTTP vs HTTPS, trailing slash variants) cannot be consolidated for crawlers.
findings.recommendation: Add <link rel='canonical' href='https://www.ssonetwork.com/events-workx'> inside <head> once the page is live.
findings.fix_prompt: Insert <link rel='canonical' href='https://www.ssonetwork.com/events-workx'> as the first link element inside <head>.

findings.issue: No viewport meta tag is present. This will cause mobile rendering failures and is a Core Web Vitals / mobile-usability ranking signal.
findings.recommendation: Add <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'> inside <head>.
findings.fix_prompt: Insert <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'> inside <head> as part of the standard HTML template.

findings.issue: og:title, og:description, and og:image are all absent. Social shares of this URL will render with no preview, severely reducing click-through from social channels.
findings.recommendation: Add complete Open Graph meta tags once the page content is confirmed. Include a high-quality event image (minimum 1200×630px) for og:image.
findings.fix_prompt:
Add the following inside <head> once live page content is confirmed:
<meta property='og:type' content='event'>
<meta property='og:title' content='WorkX 2026 | Future of Work Summit – SSO Network'>
<meta property='og:description' content='[Match improved meta description]'>
<meta property='og:image' content='[Absolute URL to 1200x630 event image]'>
<meta property='og:url' content='https://www.ssonetwork.com/events-workx'>

findings.issue: The only H1 is '403 Forbidden'. There is no event content, no keyword-relevant headings, no speaker information, no agenda, no date/venue copy, and no registration CTA — all of which are critical for search-intent alignment and conversion.
findings.recommendation: Restore the full event page content. The H1 should reflect the event name and value proposition. Body copy must cover event topics, speakers, dates, venue, and registration to satisfy informational and transactional search intent.
findings.fix_prompt: Once the 403 is resolved, ensure the H1 reads something like 'WorkX 2026: Advancing the Future of Shared Services & Operations' and that below-the-fold content includes agenda highlights, confirmed speakers, event date/location, and a prominent registration CTA above the fold per brand configuration.

findings.issue: No Event structured data is present. This prevents rich-result eligibility (event rich snippets in Google Search and Google Events carousel).
findings.recommendation: Add schema.org Event JSON-LD once real page content is confirmed. A placeholder template is provided in event_schema_jsonld below — all null fields MUST be populated from live page content before publishing.
findings.fix_prompt: Insert the JSON-LD block from the event_schema_jsonld field in this response as a <script type='application/ld+json'> element inside <head>, replacing all null values with confirmed facts from the live page before deployment.

findings.issue: No robots meta tag is declared. While absence defaults to index/follow, best practice for event microsites is to explicitly declare indexing intent and verify robots.txt does not inadvertently disallow the path.
findings.recommendation: Add <meta name='robots' content='index, follow'> and confirm /events-workx is not blocked in robots.txt.
findings.fix_prompt: Add <meta name='robots' content='index, follow'> inside <head>. Fetch https://www.ssonetwork.com/robots.txt and confirm no Disallow rule matches /events-workx or /events-*.
